subtype: Approach: ignoring the teasing at first [Thinking]
passage: If I say nothing, Kasper will get bored, Omar told himself on the walk to school in Rotterdam. Nobody wants to be boring, not even a bully. On Monday Kasper flicked his ear and called him "Sleepy Omar". Omar kept his eyes on his sums and said nothing. On Tuesday Kasper gave up after two tries and went back to his lunch. Omar felt lighter, almost proud. But by Friday the nickname had reached two other boys, and Kasper was back, louder, waiting at the gate. Omar's stomach tightened. Maybe saying nothing was only the first step, he thought, and not the whole plan.

qa.q: What nickname did Kasper give Omar?
What was Omar feeling on Friday when Kasper was waiting at the gate?
qa.a: Worried, because his stomach tightened as he realised that saying nothing was not enough on its own.

qa.q: What other approach could Omar add to ignoring, and why?
qa.a: He could tell a teacher what has been happening, because the nickname is spreading and an adult can act where silence alone cannot.

qa.q: How might Kasper have read Omar's silence on Monday and Tuesday?
qa.a: At first it may have felt dull, which fits Kasper giving up after two tries, but later Kasper may have taken the silence as a sign that Omar would not answer back.

grounding: A boy hopes ignoring the bully will make him lose interest; it helps briefly but the teasing continues.
